annotation.authors_or_issuer: Agência Câmara de Notícias (Câmara dos Deputados)
annotation.summary_en: Agência Câmara news report on the Chamber of Deputies' 29 September 2021 approval of Bill 21/2020, setting principles, foundations and guidelines for AI development and use in Brazil. It favours sectoral, risk-based, subsidiary regulation, fault-based liability (strict in consumer relations), and self-regulation, and was sent to the Senate.
annotation.title_clean: Câmara aprova projeto que regulamenta uso da inteligência artificial
annotation.title_en: Chamber approves bill regulating the use of artificial intelligence
key_provisions_or_claims: Bill 21/2020 sets principles, foundations and guidelines for AI in Brazil; the Union has exclusive power to legislate.
Sectoral regulators and the Central Bank are to manage risk, set rights and duties, and recognise self-regulation bodies.
Guidelines: subsidiary intervention, sectoral action, risk-based management, regulatory impact analysis, and fault-based liability.
Strict liability applies where AI is used in consumer relations, under the Consumer Defense Code.
It does not follow the EU model of banning or classifying high-risk AI in advance; the bill goes to the Senate.
